page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highcpu-288 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an Intel Xeon 6985P-C processor. It features 288 vCPUs mapped to 144 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The instance is equipped with 576 GB of dedicated RAM, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. It lacks local storage and integrated GPUs, relying entirely on network-attached storage. The CPU architecture includes advanced vector and matrix extensions such as AVX-512 and Intel AMX (tile and int8), alongside hardware-accelerated cryptography and virtualization support.

Benchmark results place this instance in the top tier for multi-core processing and memory bandwidth. The stress-ng multi-core CPU test yielded a score of 312098.53, while the PassMark CPU score reached 177439.07, both ranking in the top 10% of tested hardware. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with cached read-only small block speeds of 22984.49 GB/sec and uncached large block write speeds of 448.45 GB/sec. Single-core performance is moderate, with a stress-ng single-core score of 2295.49, indicating that workloads must be highly parallelized to fully exploit the hardware.

This instance is highly suited for compute-intensive, highly parallelized workloads such as software compilation, ray tracing, and large-scale database operations, as evidenced by a Geekbench clang compilation score of 70191.0 and a PassMark database operations score of 38361.83. It also demonstrates strong performance in LLM inference prompt processing, handling up to 289.28 tokens/sec for a 7B model, though text generation speeds are comparatively lower. Given its high core density and specialized instruction sets, the c4-highcpu-288 offers high qualitative cost efficiency for enterprise-scale parallel processing and static web serving, where resource utilization can be maximized across all 288 vCPUs.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4-highcpu-288 is a compute-optimized instance featuring 288 vCPUs and 576 GB of RAM, powered by a 2.3 GHz Intel Xeon 6985P-C processor with 144 physical cores. It utilizes the x86_64 architecture and includes advanced instruction sets like AVX-512 and Intel AMX. The instance lacks local storage and GPUs. Benchmark data highlights top-tier multi-core performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 312098.53 and a PassMark CPU score of 177439.07. It delivers exceptional memory bandwidth, reaching 1088.77 GB/sec for uncached large block reads, and excels in parallel tasks like software compilation and database operations. While single-core performance is average, its massive core density makes it highly cost-efficient for highly parallelized enterprise workloads, static web serving, and LLM prompt processing.
